title: Pool cycle investigation logbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log for the dedicated GPU pool cycling/thrash incident observed Nov 2-3 2025. Goal is to capture commands run, raw snippets, timeline, initial hypotheses, and short next steps so SRE/infra can action. This is a scratchpad - choppy notes, not formal postmortem.

High level summary:
- Symptom: client requests experienced intermittent 500s and large latency spikes when Dedicated pool autoscaler was active; observed repeated evict/allocate cycles and a high rate of warm misses.
- Window: Nov 2 05:10 - Nov 3 02:40 UTC (right after midnight UTC scale window).
- Impact: ~12% error rate for a 30m window for some customers, tail latency spikes 2-3x for 45m.

Key observations and metrics captured while debugging:
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale down + scale up actions with ~30-45s between events (too fast).
- Warm start miss rate spiked to 78% during the worst window. Baseline is ~8-12%.
- Average GPU attach time measured ~86s during incident (normally 30-40s).
- Metric gating: scale-down decided when active_concurrency < 2 for 20s; scale-up triggered when pending_requests > 5. These thresholds produced ping-pong given workload burstiness.

Commands I ran (timestamps in UTC local to monitor shell):
2025-11-03T00:12:09Z: kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=dedicated -o wide
- saw many pods in Terminating state then new pods in Pending in quick succession

2025-11-03T00:14:03Z: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler --since=2h | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -i scale
- repeated lines: scaleDown target=dedicated count=1 reason=low-concurrency cooldown=30s
- shortly after: scaleUp target=dedicated count=1 reason=pending-queue cooldown=10s

2025-11-03T00:17:51Z: curl -s http://metrics.internal:9100/metrics | grep warm_start_miss_rate
- warm_start_miss_rate 0.78

2025-11-03T00:18:05Z: kubectl -n dedicated logs pod/dedicated-worker-abc -c runtime | tail -n 40\- [2025-11-03T00:17:43Z] WARN warm-cache miss for model t5-xl sequence 1024
- [2025-11-03T00:17:44Z] ERROR failed attach GPU: attach timeout after 90s
- [2025-11-03T00:17:44Z] INFO falling back to cpu-ephemeral (degraded perf)

2025-11-03T00:22:12Z: kubectl -n infra get hpa autoscaler -o yaml | yq .spec  (inspected HPA thresholds)
- minReplicas: 1, maxReplicas: 40, metrics: custom metric pending_requests threshold 5

Observational notes and raw snippets:
- Pattern: scaleDown fires quickly when concurrency dips for short bursts; scaleUp sees a sudden pending backlog and requests GPU-backed pods, but attach/warmup time is long so pending queue persists and more scaleUp triggers. After queues clear, scaleDown happens, repeat.
- I noticed attach timeout error lines in runtime logs matching scaleUp windows: "ERROR failed attach GPU: attach timeout after 90s". That aligns with longer-than-normal node provisioning/attach latency in the region.
- Some nodes reported kernel driver reconnects in node syslog (short-lived): dmesg snippet showed NVLINK recoveries and nvidia-driver reinit, which correlates to extra attach latency for 2 out of 14 affected hosts.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler cooldown and thresholds are too aggressive for this workload pattern. Because scaleDown cooldown 30s and scaleUp cooldown 10s allow repeated oscillation during bursty traffic.
2) Node-level variability: a small subset of hosts are flaky (driver recovers) causing attach slowdowns that increase warm miss rate and trigger repeated scale ups.
3) Batching of scale decisions across different controllers caused double-scaling (autoscaler + cluster-autoscaler) — conflicting controllers made contradictory decisions.
4) Workload shifts: sudden increase in long-sequence requests (>=1024 tokens) increased per-request GPU warmup/kv-cache load making warm-start slower and prolonging the pending queue.

Why this is different from prior incidents:
- Prior warmup incidents usually had consistent attach time but higher cold starts due to zero baseline. Here attach failures and kernel-level host flakiness is a new signal. Also the HPA thresholds were tuned for steady traffic, not for high-frequency short bursts.

Quick mitigation we applied during the incident (temp):
- Increased minReplicas for dedicated pool from 1 -> 3 at 00:35 UTC to reduce scale-down frequency. Immediate drop in thrash but increased cost.
- Bumped scaleDown cooldown from 30s -> 180s (manual change in k8s autoscaler deployment) which stabilized oscillation.
- Triage: cordoned 3 suspect hosts and rebalanced nodes out of pool; replacement hosts came up with healthy driver logs.

Follow-ups and long-term actions (todo):
- Short term config changes (ops): set minReplicas to 2-4 depending on customer usage, increase scaleDown cooldown to 120-180s, and add jitter to scaleDown decision to avoid synchronized decisions across regions.
- Improve metrics: add "attach_latency_p95" and per-host attach failure counters to metrics so we can quickly detect host-level degradations instead of seeing only pool-level warm_miss_rate.
- Autoscaler logic changes: add hysteresis window and require sustained pending_requests > threshold for 60s before scaleUp; or use rate-based scaling tied to new request rate metric instead of instantaneous queue depth.
- Implement warm prefetch for sequences commonly seen in affected customers (identify via qps-per-model and pre-warm their KV caches during predicted windows).
- Root cause host investigation: channel host IDs to infra, check kernel driver versions, and patch hosts that show NV driver flaky behavior.
- Add a Canary mode for autoscaler config so we can test new cooldown thresholds on a small subset of traffic before global rollout.

Open questions I still have:
- What triggered the driver flakiness on the subset of hosts? Was it a rolling patch, a noisy neighbor, or thermal event? Need SRE host-level telemetry.
- Exact request distribution during the 05:10-05:40 window — I have partial logs but need sanitized request histograms to correlate token length spikes.
- Did cluster-autoscaler or any other controller attempt node-level scale concurrently and contribute to oscillation? Need controller action logs.

Immediate next steps for me:
- Share this log with infra/SRE and tag Diego/Priya on the Linear ticket linked above.
- Add a Grafana dashboard panel for attach latency p50/p95 (work with metrics team) and a per-host attach-fail heatmap.
- Draft a short runbook update: if warm_start_miss_rate > 40% and attach_p95 > 60s, set minReplicas=3 and pause scaleDown for 5m.

Notes to self (loose):
- Be careful when changing cooldowns globally; try canary first.
- If kernel driver causes recurring problems, consider nightly host rotation rather than live remediation to reduce customer impact.

Raw command history excerpt (for reproducibility):
- kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=dedicated -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler --since=3h | grep -E "scaleUp|scaleDown" -n
- curl -s http://metrics.internal:9100/metrics | grep -E "warm_start_miss_rate|attach_latency"
- kubectl -n dedicated logs -l app=runtime --tail=200 | sed -n '1,400p' | grep -i attach

End log.

If anything else to add, will append here. This should be sufficient to hand off to SRE/infra as a breadcrumbs artifact.
